record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: If t is a Sturmian word of slope alpha, must the least period of every nonempty factor of t belong to Pi(alpha)?

evidence.quote: Let t denote a Sturmian word with slope alpha. If a word is a nonempty factor of t, then its least period belongs to Pi(alpha).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let α ∈ (0,1) be an irrational number with continued fraction expansion α = [0; 1+d₁, d₂, d₃, …] (with dᵢ ≥ 1 for i ≥ 2 and d₁ ≥ 0). Define the standard sequence of finite words over {a, b} by

  s₋₁ = b,  s₀ = a,  sₙ = sₙ₋₁^{dₙ} sₙ₋₂  for n ≥ 1,

and let qₙ = |sₙ|, so q₋₁ = 1, q₀ = 1, qₙ = dₙ qₙ₋₁ + qₙ₋₂. Define

  Π(α) = { j·qₙ + qₙ₋₁ : n ≥ 0 and 1 ≤ j ≤ dₙ₊₁ } ⊂ ℤ₊,

i.e. the set of denominators of all (principal and intermediate) convergents of α.

A Sturmian word of slope α is any infinite word t over a two-letter alphabet whose factor complexity satisfies p_t(n) = n+1 for every n ≥ 1 and whose letter frequencies are α and 1−α. The least period of a nonempty finite word w = w₁w₂…w_m is the smallest positive integer p such that wᵢ = wᵢ₊ₚ for every 1 ≤ i ≤ m − p.

Question: For every Sturmian word t of slope α, and every nonempty factor w of t, does the least period of w belong to Π(α)?
artifact.status_search_result: Currie and Saari, in "Least Periods of Factors of Infinite Words" (RAIRO – Theor. Inform. Appl., 2008), explicitly characterize the set of least periods of factors of a Sturmian word of slope α, confirming that every such least period belongs to the set of denominators of (semi)convergents of α (and that for the Fibonacci word this set is exactly the Fibonacci numbers). Subsequent work (e.g., "Standard factors of Sturmian words", 2010) builds on this characterization.

status_evidence.title: Least Periods of Factors of Infinite Words (Currie, Saari)
status_evidence.snippet: We characterize the set of least periods of factors of a Sturmian word; for the Fibonacci word this set is the set of Fibonacci numbers.
status_evidence.claim: The set of least periods of factors of a Sturmian word of slope α is characterized, resolving the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Standard factors of Sturmian words
status_evidence.snippet: Follow-up work refining the description of factors and periods of Sturmian words.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature treats the periods set of Sturmian factors as known.
